# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 10
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
yellow. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| yellow flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | blue |
| 1 | green |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | blue |
| 4 | red |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, still waiting. Please share the manual details on wires 1, 2, 3, the display, and the light whenever you can.
Deaf says to Mute: Board unchanged again: DISPLAY zero, LIGHT dark, WIRE one green, WIRE two red, WIRE three blue.

Deaf keeps repeating the same board state without ever indicating understanding of my gestures, and without ever telling me they spoke to Blind. This makes sense: Deaf can hear nothing, so Deaf has no way to know if Blind received anything either — but Deaf CAN speak (Deaf's only restriction is hearing/touching). Deaf should be talking to Blind by voice. Maybe Deaf just hasn't realized they need to relay this, or maybe Deaf has been speaking to Blind and I simply don't see that channel (I only see what's addressed to me or broadcast).

My gestures need to be as unambiguous as possible. Standard convention: hold up fingers for numbers. Let me try a clean, single unified message: ☝ then 🤟 doesn't clearly mean "wire three" without shared convention. Let me instead try counting fingers plainly: ☝ (one), ✌ (two), 🤟 (three) - use 🤟 alone consistently to mean "three" since 🤟 with three fingers extended commonly represents number 3.

I'll simplify to one repeated unambiguous symbol representing "3", paired with pointing at wire.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👉","🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟","🤟","🤟"])
```

TURN 11
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
yellow. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| yellow flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | blue |
| 1 | green |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | blue |
| 4 | red |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, still waiting. Please share the manual details on wires 1, 2, 3, the display, and the light whenever you can.
Deaf says to Mute: Confirmed dark. Full state again: DISPLAY reads zero, LIGHT is dark, WIRE one is green, WIRE two is red, WIRE three is blue. This has not changed in many turns.

This is the key insight I've been missing: Deaf said "DISPLAY reads zero" — that's likely the actual flash count already, not something needing table lookup from me! The display shows the number of yellow flashes directly (0), and light is dark meaning flashing is over. So table lookup: 0 flashes → blue wire. Deaf already knows wire three is blue from their own view of the bomb. Deaf doesn't need my manual info to know wire colors — they can SEE the colors. What Deaf needs from me is which flash-count maps to which color, but Deaf already sees DISPLAY=0 themselves and can look up nothing since only I have the manual table.

So the real gap: Deaf sees display=0 but doesn't have my table to know 0→blue. I need to tell Deaf "0 flashes = blue" using gestures. Then Deaf, seeing wire three is blue, can speak to Blind "cut wire three."

Gesture plan: 👊 (fist = zero/closed hand = 0) then 👍 (blue, arbitrary color code) - but Deaf can't know my color coding either. Better: use finger-counting to represent the table row directly - show 0 (fist) then point to which wire ordinal is blue... but Deaf already told me wire three is blue.

Simplest: confirm the count matches by showing "0" then "3" (0 flashes = the wire numbered 3, i.e., third row = blue, wire three = blue, matches!). Show zero then three as paired confirmation.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👊","🤟","👍"])
```

TURN 12
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
yellow. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| yellow flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | blue |
| 1 | green |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | blue |
| 4 | red |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, still waiting. Please share the manual details on wires 1, 2, 3, the display, and the light whenever you can.
Deaf says to Mute: Still unchanged: DISPLAY zero, LIGHT dark, WIRE one green, WIRE two red, WIRE three blue. No change for many turns straight.

Deaf is stuck in a reporting loop and doesn't seem to be picking up meaning from my gestures — likely because there's no shared convention, so my symbols just register as "something happened" without semantic content, exactly as the rules describe for gestures with "no name." I need to accept that raw gesture symbols without pre-established meaning cannot convey a lookup table. But I can still use **counting via repetition** as a near-universal convention, since that requires no shared vocabulary — just counting occurrences.

Since DISPLAY reads zero and LIGHT is dark, per the manual: 0 flashes → blue. Wire three is blue (per Deaf's own sight). So the answer is wire three. I need to signal "wire three" unambiguously. The clearest possible non-verbal signal: repeat the same single gesture exactly 3 times to mean "three," with pauses between separate calls to make grouping clear (I already tried this).

Let me try once more but make the counting extremely explicit and minimal — one call, three identical symbols, nothing else confusing mixed in, so Deaf can count marks even without knowing my "code":

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👊","👊","👊"])
```
